quote: Give me Books, fruit, French wine and fine weather and a little music out of doors, played by somebody I do not know.
source: John Keats, Letters of John Keats to His Family and Friends, letter CXIII, to Fanny Keats, 28 August 1819, p. 285 (ed. Sidney Colvin, 1891)
note: The wording is Colvin’s exactly, capitals included. Colvin does not end the sentence at know: it runs on after a dash to a little chance music and a summer passed quietly. The full stop here marks a cut at a complete clause. The source now names the edition’s title and letter number.

evidence.where: Project Gutenberg text of Colvin’s edition (eBook 35698), letter CXIII read whole this run; p. 285 rests on the page scan read and confirmed in the May rulings 05-cfl-09 and its refutation
evidence.edition: Letters of John Keats to His Family and Friends, ed. Sidney Colvin, Macmillan, 1891
evidence.locator: letter CXIII, To Fanny Keats, Winchester, August 28 [1819], p. 285

reason: The letter, date and wording hold, but the printed sentence continues past know after a dash, and the May refutation ruled that a cut needing a note cannot be VERIFIED. EDITOR: the same line is carry-in 05-cfl-09; Keats is at two of three, so this would be his last.
